s: Der Fuchs ist für seine List bekannt.
The fox is known for its cunning.
Das Trojanische Pferd ist eine berühmte List.
The Trojan Horse is a famous ruse.
List.et: From Middle High German list, from Old High German list, from Proto-West Germanic *listi, from Proto-Germanic *listiz. Cognate with English list (“craft, cunning”), which see for more.
From Middle High German list, from Old High German list, from Proto-West Germanic *listi, from Proto-Germanic *listiz. Cognate with English list (“craft, cunning”), which see for more.

Lisztäffchen.et: From Liszt + Äffchen, because the white mane of this monkey species resembles the hair of composer Franz Liszt.

s: a female given name from Elisabeth
Mein Name steht auf der Liste.
My name is on the list.
Liste.et: 16th century, from Italian lista, itself of Germanic origin, whence also the inherited doublet Leiste (“skirting board”). Cognate with Dutch lijst and English list.

Lissabon.et: Ultimately from Arabic لِشْبُونَة (lišbūna), from Latin Olisipo, further etymology uncertain.

s: a female given name from Elisabeth
… das einzige Kind der armen Lisbeth! … Der Kerl gab mir ein schönes Gebot auf Lisbeth, …
a female given name, a less common variant of Lieselotte
cottontop tamarin, Pinché tamarin, Saguinus oedipus, a New World monkey

Liss.et: From Polish Lis, Ukrainian Лис (Lys), Belarusian Ліс (Lis), Russian Лис (Lis), and Czech Lis. Ultimately, from Proto-Slavic *lisъ (“fox”).

s: a female given name, an Austrian variant of Liesl and Liesel

lispeln.et: From Old High German lispen (“lisp”) + -eln, ultimately from onomatopoeic Proto-Germanic *wlispaz (“stammering, lisping”).

Liska.et: From Czech Liška, from liška (“fox”) or Slovak Líška, from líška (“fox”). The meaning is equivalent to the native surname Fuchs.

Lischka.et: From Czech Liška, from liška (“fox”) or Slovak Líška, from líška (“fox”).

s: Die Lisztomanie, die gegenwärtig in Paris grassirt, ist ein beliebtes Thema zu Satyren der Pariser Feuilletons.
Lisztomanie.et: Coined by German poet, writer and literary critic Heinrich Heine in 1844, from Liszt + -o- + -manie.
